newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, then slips on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, then slips on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, driven by firmer physical prices and some shortcovering, ended higher Wednesday in sluggish trade, then slipped on ACCESS after a bearish weekly inventory report.

July climbed 5.4 cents to close at $2.157 per million British thermal units, then in after-hours trade retreated to the $2.12-2.13 area. August settled 4.5 cents higher at $2.168. Other months ended up by 0.3 to 3.7 cents.
"We saw a technical bounce today, but the AGA number was bearish. It was out of the range. I'd hit the bid," said one East Coast trader.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 93 bcf, well-above expectations in the 80-85 bcf range. Overall stocks are 217 bcf, or 22 percent, over year-ago. Eastern storage gained 62 bcf and was still 107 bcf, or 23 percent, above last year.
While few expected paper prices to crumble below the $2 mark, most expected mild weather this week to keep the market on the defensive.
Some said forecasts next week for more heat in the Southwest and some above-normal weather in Texas and the South could stir some buying.
Temperatures in the Midwest and East are again expected to range from normal to below normal next week.

Technical traders agreed the market was due for a bounce after a four-day 10 percent sell-off. They pegged July support at Tuesday's low of $2.08 and then at $2.05 and $2.00. Resistance was seen at $2.21, $2.25, $2.37-2.38 and the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed Wednesday by more than five cents to the mid-teens. Midcon pipes were several cents higher in the low-$2s. New York city gate prices gained a few cents to about $2.40.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 3.7 cents to $2.233. NYMEX said 27,197 contracts traded, down sharply from Tuesday's revised tally of 51,012.
On KCBT, July finished 4.6 cents higher at $2.008, while deferreds ended mixed. The East/West spread widened by 0.9 cent to 14.9 cents (NYMEX premium).
